questions.title: How does the local softmax in FlashAttention-3 guarantee exact equivalence to full softmax?
questions.question_body: The paper states that FlashAttention-3 uses a local softmax with running rowwise maxima and sums, similar to FlashAttention-2, and remains exact (no approximation) while avoiding materializing S and P in HBM. I’ve seen the high-level argument in FA-2, but I’m struggling to reconstruct the exact invariants used here when pipelining and overlapping GEMMs with softmax. Specifically: when the algorithm updates per-row running values m_i and l_i across blocks j, how is numerical equivalence preserved given the interleaving of WGMMA, exponentials, and rescalings? Could someone provide a concise derivation showing that the streamed computation still produces O = softmax(QK^T)V exactly, i.e., that the blockwise updates of m_i and l_i maintain the same normalization as the full softmax computed at once?

questions.title: What exactly is being overlapped in the 2-stage pipeline, and what depends on what?
questions.question_body: In Algorithm 2 (consumer warpgroup), the main loop overlaps the WGMMA for Q_i K_j^T with the softmax derived from S_next, and also overlaps the WGMMA for P_cur V_{j-1}. I’m confused about the dependency ordering: which waits guarantee correctness, and which steps are safe to execute without waiting? Could someone annotate the loop with a dependency graph indicating when S_cur, P_cur, S_next, and O_i are valid, and why it’s safe to compute softmax for the next block while the previous P_cur V_{j-1} is still in flight?

questions.title: How does pingpong scheduling across warpgroups ensure the MFU work (exp) is hidden under Tensor Core GEMMs?
questions.question_body: The paper claims that using bar.sync to force GEMMs in warpgroup 1 to run before GEMMs in warpgroup 2 leads to the softmax of warpgroup 1 being overlapped with GEMMs of warpgroup 2, and then the roles swap. Could someone explain in more detail how this ordering is enforced in practice, given that NVCC and the scheduler may reorder? For instance, what exact barriers and instruction placements are required so MFU-bound work ends up concurrently issued with WGMMA, and how is fairness between the two warpgroups maintained to avoid starvation?

questions.title: What are SS-GEMM and RS-GEMM in Algorithm 1 and how do they map to WGMMA operand placement?
questions.question_body: Algorithm 1 labels two GEMMs as SS-GEMM and RS-GEMM, with a note that SS or RS indicates whether the first operand is sourced from shared memory or registers. In Hopper’s WGMMA model, operands can come from SMEM or RMEM depending on instruction variants. Could someone clarify the operand layouts and sources for these two GEMMs, and how this choice affects register pressure and shared memory traffic for the QK^T and PV products respectively?

questions.title: Why does FP8 WGMMA require k-major operands in SMEM, and how does that constrain V tiling?
questions.question_body: Section 2.2 says FP8 WGMMA only accepts k-major in SMEM for operands, while FP16 WGMMA is more flexible. For the second GEMM involving V, this implies V tiles in SMEM must be contiguous in the K dimension. Could someone explain the hardware reason for this FP8 constraint, and concretely how it affects the tile shapes and strides chosen for V in the attention kernel? A small example with M, N, K and the resulting SMEM tile strides would help.

questions.title: How does the in-kernel transpose for FP8 using LDSM/STSM actually work on packed 8-bit data?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions using LDSM/STSM (ldmatrix/stmatrix) to transpose FP8 tiles in shared memory, packing two 8-bit elements into the 16-bit granularity, and then doing some register moves because the transpose variants cannot split the packed bytes. Could someone give a minimal schematic of the steps: (1) load with LDSM, (2) register shuffles/permutations required to separate or reorder bytes, and (3) store with STSM, showing how an example 16x16 FP8 tile is transposed without excessive register use?

questions.title: What is the exact register permutation needed to make the FP8 accumulator layout feed the next FP8 WGMMA?
questions.question_body: Section 3.3 says the FP32 accumulator layout of FP8 WGMMA does not match the A-operand layout expected by the next FP8 WGMMA, so a byte permute is applied to reorder bytes as {d0 d1 d4 d5 d2 d3 d6 d7}, repeated every 8 bytes. Could someone explain: (a) which dimensions this reorders logically in the P tile, (b) why this particular pattern, and (c) how this interacts with the in-kernel transpose’s row permutation for V so that the final PV product is correct without cross-thread shuffles?

questions.title: How does block quantization change the softmax scaling, and what is actually rescaled where?
questions.question_body: With block quantization, Q, K, V are quantized per block with their own scales. The paper says the algorithm can "scale each block of S" to account for this with no extra compute. Could someone spell out the formulas? If Q_block = q_scale * Q_fp8 and K_block = k_scale * K_fp8, then S_block = Q_block K_block^T = (q_scale k_scale) (Q_fp8 K_fp8^T). How and where is the factor q_scale k_scale folded into the streamed softmax updates of m_i and l_i, and how are P V products rescaled to remain consistent with the final O?

questions.title: Why does incoherent processing with random orthogonal M reduce FP8 quantization error without changing attention?
questions.question_body: Section 3.3 introduces multiplying both Q and K by the same random orthogonal matrix M (constructed via Hadamard and random sign flips), arguing that (QM)(KM)^T = QK^T keeps attention scores unchanged while reducing outliers before FP8 quantization. Can someone provide an intuition or a short argument for why this reduces the peak magnitudes at FP8 quantization time? Also, are there corner cases where M could worsen quantization (e.g., when outliers are structured across features)?

questions.title: How is numerical stability preserved when overlapping softmax with concurrent GEMMs?
questions.question_body: The 2-stage pipeline overlaps softmax computations (which involve exp and reductions) with asynchronous WGMMA. Given possible latency and reorderings, is there any risk that partial rescalings of O_i are applied before all dependent values are finalized? Which specific waits and barriers guarantee that the running max m_i and sum l_i are consistent for each row, and that O_i receives the correct rescaling factor diag(exp(m_old - m))^{-1} at exactly the right time?

questions.title: What is the exact FLOPs accounting used for the forward and backward passes?
questions.question_body: The paper uses 4 * seqlen^2 * head_dim * nheads FLOPs for the forward pass (halved for causal masks) and multiplies by 2.5 for the backward pass. Could someone derive the 4 factor for forward (is it precisely 2 GEMMs counting multiply-add as 2 FLOPs?), and the 2.5 factor for backward (from 5 matmuls vs 2 in forward)? Also, does the FLOPs counting include softmax exp, reductions, and rescalings, or are those excluded as non-GEMM FLOPs?

questions.title: How does setmaxnreg practically help with warp-specialization, and what are the trade-offs?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions using setmaxnreg to realloc registers such that producer warps (mostly issuing TMA) get fewer registers, while consumer warps (doing WGMMA and softmax) get more. Could someone explain how this is orchestrated in a CTA with multiple warpgroups? How do you decide the register budget split, and what are the failure modes (e.g., spills due to too small budgets on producers, or occupancy loss on consumers)?

questions.title: What determines the choice of block sizes B_r and B_c under register and SMEM constraints?
questions.question_body: Choosing B_r (rows of Q per CTA) and B_c (K,V tiles) affects register pressure (e.g., storing S_next of size B_r x B_c) and SMEM usage (circular buffers of size s). How do you practically pick B_r and B_c on H100 to balance: (a) WGMMA tile efficiency, (b) space for multiple stages s in SMEM, (c) register headroom for the 2-stage pipeline without spills, and (d) occupancy? Any recommended heuristics or rules of thumb for head dimensions d in {64, 128, 256}?

questions.title: Why does FA-3 FP16 match or beat cuDNN at long sequences but FP8 lags in some masked cases?
questions.question_body: The results indicate FA-3 FP16 outperforms or matches cuDNN for large seqlen, while FP8 is competitive but can lag for some head dims under causal masking. The discussion mentions the lack of a persistent kernel for FP8. Could someone expand on how persistence and load-balancing specifically impact small or masked workloads, and what kernel design changes would be needed to close the gap for FP8 under causal attention?

questions.title: How is backward pass adapted to the asynchronous/pipelined design, especially for dsoftmax?
questions.question_body: The paper focuses on the forward pass algorithm and mentions the backward in a later section. For the backward, dS = dsoftmax(dP) involves rowwise reductions dependent on P, and dQ, dK, dV each involve GEMMs. How are the producer-consumer split, circular buffers, and 2-stage (or 3-stage) pipelining applied in backward so that reductions in dsoftmax are overlapped with GEMMs, while preserving numerical stability with running max/rescale if needed? Any notable differences from the forward overlap strategy?
